paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases, comparing two large vision-language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Reasoning Steps," is on a linear scale ranging from 5 to 40, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Pass@1 Rate (%)", is also linear, ranging from 0 to 100 with tick marks every 20 units. Two lines are plotted: GPT-4o is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, and Claude-3.5-Sonnet is shown as a dashed light purple line with cross markers. At 5 reasoning steps, GPT-4o achieves a Pass@1 rate of 6.5%, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet reaches 19.4%. At 10 steps, the rates increase to 32.3% for GPT-4o and 38.7% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. At 20 steps, the performance further improves to 77.4% for GPT-4o and 87.1% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. At 40 steps, the rates reach 83.9% for GPT-4o and 89.2% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet. Both models show a significant improvement in performance with increasing reasoning steps, but the gains appear to plateau after 20 steps, with diminishing returns at 40 steps.
